cards.body:
## Summary
Math Buddy decides what KIND of item it is looking at (a linear equation the model wrote, a Calculus spec, a school unit's spec) by three different mechanisms at 15 lines in 7 files, and four marking loops carry the same scaffold. One registry (`rules/kinds.ts`) and one pure judge replace them: a sheet is read by the model, judged per item in code, and recorded once.

## Description
The decision that is the product (is this answer right, which slip, what may the desk say) is made by whichever file asks, in its own way. The photo path chooses a marker for the whole sheet (`mark.ts:158-159`), the typed path chooses per item (`mark.ts:328`), the explainer re-detects from the item (`explain.ts:196`), the hint chooses its stance from the learner's path (`hint.ts:57-58`) but its leak check and fallback line from the question's text (`hint.ts:65,77,106`), the generator from the topic (`items.ts:123-124`).

The cost is visible two ways. First, behaviour: probed on the current tree, the same three strings on the same mixed sheet are marked right, wrong, right when typed and right, wrong, unsure when photographed; a school-path learner's derivative question gets the linear-equations stance ('factoring and linear-equations unit; prefer the unit's methods over heavier ones') while its leak check already reads it as Calculus; a Calculus-path learner's fractions task gets the Calculus I stance. Second, change cost: a fourth kind (or the Phase 2 placement staircase, which judges single items of many kinds with no practice set, `mathsRows.ts:55`) means editing 7 files, copying a fifth marking loop and re-deciding the kind by a fourth mechanism.

The move: `rules/kinds.ts` holds `kindOfSpec(spec)`, `kindOfQuestion(text)` and `kindOfTopic(topicId)` (all pure, built on the existing `isCalcSpec`, `isSchoolSpec`, the two `specFromQuestion` readers and `pathOfTopic`), and `judgeItem(item, read, ctx)` / `judgeSet(practice, reads, ctx)`, the one decision. `mark.ts` keeps the model half (three reading prompts and schemas, unchanged) and returns `Read[]`; `judgeSet` settles each item by ITS kind; `markTyped` builds its reads from the typed strings; `land()` is called once. A linear read that carries the model's own solution keeps today's rule (the solution must hold, else the desk asks); a linear read with no solution field is judged by the code's own root (`rootOf`, not degenerate), which is exactly what typed marking does today. The explainer's spoken-value settle (`settle`) stays as it is; only its kind detection and leak dispatch move onto the registry. The hint's stance follows the item's kind where the text reads, and falls back to the learner's path only where it does not; the voice stays the learner's.

## Flow
- Phone photographs or types -> `/api/mark` -> `markSet` (reader by sheet kind, unchanged prompts) or `markTyped` -> `judgeSet` -> `land` -> `practice.marked`: nothing the TV or the phone sees changes shape.
- Homework hint -> `kindOfQuestion(item.text)` picks stance, leak rule, unit name and withheld line from one answer; `api/hint` asks the same function for the lesson library.
- `makeItems` -> `kindOfTopic` replaces the two inline `pathOfTopic` tests.
- Future: a placement item is `judgeItem` with a spec and an answer, no sheet.

## Expected impact
Four marking loops become one judge plus three readers (mark.ts 372 lines to roughly 240); the kind is decided by one module instead of 15 lines in 7 files; typed and photographed marking of the same strings cannot disagree for any mix of kinds, which today is pinned for school sets only; two real prompt mismatches in the hint close; and the Phase 2 placement staircase and card B's second go get a single-item entry point instead of a private function.

## Evaluation
Claim: one registry and one pure judge make marking, explaining and hinting agree on an item's kind, closing a typed-versus-photo disagreement and a hint-stance mismatch that probes show today, without changing any screen or stored shape.
Before: 0 of 7 behaviour cases pass (case 6 is a declared GUARD, green before by design); probe: typed marks a mixed sheet right, wrong, right and photo marks it right, wrong, unsure; mark.ts has 4 loops, 4 land() calls, 3 byN maps, 4 unsure++ sites.
After: 7 of 7 behaviour cases pass and the guard stays green; school-marking, calc-marking, calc-hint, maths-rules, school-stretch suites unchanged and green; 1 land() call in mark.ts.
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: architecture

cards.body:
## Summary
On Math Buddy's Walk, a ringed item is a dead end: the pen shows where it broke and the learner can do nothing with that on the desk. Give a wrong item ONE typed second go on the phone; code judges it, the TV draws the result as a picture (the ring now wears a tick) and the record keeps the honest first attempt.

## Description
Today the loop after a slip is: look where the pen is, rework on paper, then either press Six more (a brand new set; the same question never returns) or describe it by voice, which can only rename the slip. The desk never learns that the learner fixed it, and the learner never learns whether the fix holds. Essay Master already closes this loop for sentences (rewrite in place, the move inks, a ghost arrow shows the before and after); Math Buddy, whose whole pitch is that the pen shows the line, does not.

The data and the judge are already there. `typedSettle` judges one typed answer for every item kind with no model call; the item carries its slip and pen position; the Lamplight vocabulary already has the ring and the earned tick. The move: a wrong item with no second go may take one typed answer from the phone (`POST /api/second`, `{n, answer}`); code decides (`typedSettle`), an unreadable answer is refused in a desk sentence and does not spend the go; the route raises one server-only event `practice.second {n, verdict}`, which carries a verdict and never the typed answer; the reducer sets `second: 'right' | 'wrong'` once and leaves verdict, slip, pen, history, digest and the learner record exactly as marking wrote them (a second go is practice, not evidence, the same ruling `reviseSentence` makes for essays).

On the TV nothing asks for typing and nothing new is said: on the Sheet and the Walk a fixed item keeps its ring and pen (the record of where it broke) and gains the earned orange tick on its number and its tally mark; a second go that missed draws a second ring stroke. The taped card carries one short sentence in the same slot. 'To look at' counts and the first-to-look focus skip a fixed item; Tonight's hero, the landing and the recap keep reading the first attempt, so the record and every summary agree.

## Flow
- Walk on a ringed item: phone shows 'Try it again' (one box, one Send) under the voice prompt, only for a wrong item with no second go.
- Send -> `/api/second` -> `secondProblem(item)` -> `typedSettle` -> `practice.second` -> the TV redraws: ring plus tick, or a double ring.
- Back to the sheet: the head reads 'One to look at' instead of 'Two'; focus lands on the next unfixed item.
- Six more still works as before.

## Expected impact
The single most common thing a child does after a marked set (go back to the line and fix it) becomes visible: 4 steps and a lost question become 1 typed answer and one picture, inside the same Walk. It adds the missing half of the pen's promise without a point, a streak or a percentage, never puts an answer or a verdict word on the phone, and the one-go limit keeps it from becoming guess-and-check.

## Evaluation
Claim: a wrong item takes one code-judged typed second go, drawn as a picture, with the record untouched.
Before: 0 of 7 behaviour cases pass (case 8 is a declared GUARD, green before by design); a wrong item has no road to be answered again (store.ts:525-528, explain.ts:177-181).
After: 7 of 7 behaviour cases pass and the guard stays green; the existing tv-sheet, maths-tv, maths-rules, school-marking and phone-panel suites unchanged and green.
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: direction (the map's description names the marked sheet and its walk, not a second go; it falls inside STUDY-DESK-SCOPE.md's Check my work, overturned 2026-09-08). Contract consumers of the new item field and event: store.ts (type, shown, reducer, NEEDS_LEARNER), api/session/route.ts (SERVER_ONLY), tv/sheetRows.ts, maths/MathsTV.tsx, app/phone/page.tsx; not touched by design: memory.ts, rules/digest.ts, tv/landingRows.ts, tv/screens.tsx recap (they read the first attempt).
cards.evidence: store.ts:525-528 reducer: `shown(e.verdict && it.verdict === "unsure" ? {...} : !e.verdict && e.slip && it.verdict === "wrong" && slipsFor(topic).some(...) ? { ...it, slip, said, reply } : { ...it, reply })` - a wrong item can take a slip name or a reply, never a verdict. explain.ts:177-181 comment: 'renamed is set only when the item was already wrong ... Its verdict, its pen (slipAt) and the learner record are left as they were.' working.ts:58-62 lookAt returns 'Look where the pen is.' for a slipAt-placed wrong item. phone/page.tsx:459 `asking = !!item && (item.verdict === "wrong" || item.verdict === "unsure" || !!reply)` gates only the voice box. Steps today to learn whether a correction holds: finish the Walk, Back to the sheet, Down to Six more, Select, wait for a new set (school units are code-written, linear sets are a model call), work six NEW questions, snap or type, wait for marking = 6+ steps and the corrected question is gone; after: type one answer on the phone, read one picture. Four TV-side derivations of the same tally: sheetRows.ts:32, MathsTV.tsx:476, 775, 777. probe context: `typedSettle` is the proven single-item judge (maths school-marking-test.cjs test 11 pins typed == photo for school sets); mark.ts:332 already drops the pen for a typed answer, which is why the second go keeps the first attempt's pen. Never-re-propose check: challenge-2026-09-25 desk-pipelines B ('Rewrite one sentence in place') is Essay only; challenge-2026-09-25 desk-pipelines A moved pen location into rules/maths and did not add an answer-again road; no finding in the prior findings.jsonl titles mentions a second go. Hot files: store.ts is in the write set (one field, one event, one case); tv/keys.ts, tv/screens.tsx and uat/driver/linga-text.cjs are not (no new key: the TV never asks for typing). Wave note: card A rewrites mark.ts and rules go through kinds.ts; run A first, then B imports judgeItem instead of exporting typedSettle (B's mark.ts hunk is one export line and disappears).
